newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil shrs end off 1.3 pct on Telebras.
newsitem.headline: Brazil shrs end off 1.3 pct on Telebras.

text.p: Brazil stocks end off 1.3 percent on continued market nervousness about a Telebras court ruling Wednesday and rumors that the central bank was considering changes to foreign exchange policy, brokers said.
The Bovespa index of the 42 most-traded shares ended down 854 points at 65,034 points. Turnover was moderate at 469.8 million reais ($457.3 million).
"Selling pressure in Telebras is still very strong," a trader said. Telebras preferred shares fell 1.69 percent to close at 75.60 reais.
Traders said foreign investors remained on the sidelines after a court decided on Wednesday to back a Telebras subscription of 13.4 billion shares, made in 1990.
Although a final decision on the issue should not come within a year, analysts forecast that the issue could diminish Telebras share earnings by four percent.

In addition, they said rumors that the Central Bank had produced a report recommending an acceleration of the depreciation of the real currency have also increased pessimism among investors. The bank, however, denied the existence of such a report.

"It is not a Central Bank report," said Manoel Montenegro Neto, a spokesman for the Central bank. "The Central Bank acts in the market, and when it does, the market knows what the Central Bank is up to," he added.
Among other losers, power company Eletrobras preferred shares closed off 2.57 percent at 341 reais. Oil monopoly Petrobras preferred shares ended at 127.99 reais, down 1.55 percent.
Mining giant Vale do Rio Doce preferred shares, the big winner, rose 2.82 percent to close at 21.90 reais.
Sao Paulo bourse's power sector index comprising nine most liquid stocks of the electrical sector dropped 0.07 percent to close at 1,817 points, a bourse spokeswoman said.
